profile.headline: Lead Software Engineer at DraftKings Inc.
profile.summary: Hello, my name is Eric Kipnis, and I am a Lead Software Engineer at DraftKings in Boston, MA, based in the Greater Philadelphia area. As a self-driven individual with 10+ years of experience and a passion for software engineering, I take pride in challenging myself and consistently providing a customer-focused mindset with my solutions.

positions.title: Game Engineer Intern
positions.description: While on co-op at High 5 Games, I worked to overhaul the existing company gaffing tools, which are used to perform Quality Assurance testing on their slot machine games. Throughout designing and developing the newly unified gaffing tool, I collaborated with several different teams and departments to   pinpoint the necessary features to produce. Also, I consistently attended team meetings and held demonstrations of the tool to get constant feedback and improve the implemented functionality.

positions.title: Information Technology Intern
positions.description:
During my co-op I was responsible for working with several different teams in my department and attended and contributed to team meetings multiple times a week. I designed and developed several tools from start to finish using C# and .NET technologies with integrated access to various databases to aid in making specific tasks easier for other developers.

Some of these tools included a Document Text Swapper, Unresolved ID Finder and an Error Log Viewer. 

Also, I attended several intern seminars hosted by the Federal Reserve Board that helped to advance and foster leadership and teamwork.

volunteerExperiences.description:
My Life My Choice is an organization based in the Boston area that stands up against the commercial sexual exploitation of adolescents through mentorship, prevention groups, and advocacy for better public policies.

I've worked closely with My Life My Choice to develop a prototype for an internal tool (developed in Drupal) that would help to convert their current paper-based data intake process into an entirely digital one. Not only will the tool save time, but it will allow the generation of reports that can be used to showcase the statistical effectiveness of their organization and ideally allow them to gain additional funding from government grants. Eventually, the tool could be used across several of My Life My Choice's expanding sister organizations.

My responsibilities included all of the development and data modeling for the project.
